name: König Konrad der Junge
credit: No portrait is known; a monogram is shown.
bio: Konrad der Junge, known as Conradin, was the last Hohenstaufen king and was executed at Naples in 1268 at the age of sixteen; songs are ascribed to him in the Codex Manesse.
One of his songs appears here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: A Child in Years
poems.author: König Konrad der Junge
poems.text:
I joy in flowers red and bright,
Which May will yield us soon in store.
They stood but now in woful plight,
For winter brought them sorrow sore.
But now with many a joyous day
Maytide will give us recompense,
And therefore all the world is gay.

What help from summer do I get
And from the days so long and light?
My hopes of comfort all are set
On one who grieves me day and night.
That lady now would prove her worth,
If she would make me glad of heart;
Then should I come to real mirth.

When to my love I bid good-bye,
No joy in life is left me, none!
Alas, for grief I am like to die,
That such a suit was e'er begun!
A strange thing Love to me appears;
Lady, for this I suffer sorely,
That I am but a child in years!
